name: copy-prompt-button
purpose: The "Copy prompt" button of a docs or product home: one dark chip that copies a ready-made prompt for a coding agent and, after its label, shows the marks of the agents it works with (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Cursor by default). The chip carries the design system's AI treatment, the same three layers as `HighlightButton`: a blurred gradient glow rotating behind it, the brand-accent gradient over the glow, and a dark scrim over both that holds the white label at contrast; on hover the gradient and the scrim fade to a quarter and the glow blooms through. It is dark in both themes (it renders under `data-theme="dark"`), so it reads as the AI entry point next to a primary button, and a tooltip says what it does. The marks are single-colour and decorative, drawn in the chip's own ink; their names reach screen readers as the button's description ("Works with Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor"). With `closable` a dismiss button sits beside the chip, and dismissing removes both from the layout.
useWhen: Use CopyPromptButton to copy a ready-made agent prompt without showing its text; a visible value gets a CopyButton.
The hero of a documentation home or a product landing, beside the primary action (`Get started`), when the page hands its reader a prompt for their agent.
Inside `DocAgentCard`, the "Your AI agent, fluent in Azion" card of a docs home (it renders this button by default).
avoidWhen: To show the prompt text itself on the page → use `DocPrompt` (it renders the text with its own copy control).
To copy a value, a token or a code snippet → use `CopyButton`.
As a generic dark button → use `Button variant="secondary"`.
related: `DocPrompt` — the prompt rendered in full, with a copy control.
`DocAgentCard` — the docs-home card that places this button in its left column.
`DocHero` — the docs-home masthead whose `actions` slot holds `Get started` and this button.
`CopyButton` — the icon-only copy control; this button shares its clipboard fallback.
`HighlightButton` — the AI-flow button whose glow, gradient and scrim this chip shares.
`Logo` — draws an agent mark from its asset file in the chip's ink.
bestPractices: Put it second, after the primary `Button` (`Get started`), and explain what the prompt does in one line below the row (`DocHero`'s `note` slot).
Keep the default agents unless the product supports a different set; pass `:agents="[]"` to draw the label alone.
Pass the exact prompt in `value`; the button copies it as it stands.
Do not recolour the marks: they are single-colour by design and follow the chip's ink.
To draw a mark from the agent's asset file instead of the icon font, give the agent a `logo` (`@aziontech/webkit/assets/claude-symbol-color.svg`); `Logo` flattens it to the chip's ink.

Set `closable` where the chip is guidance the reader can put away (a first-use overview), not where it is part of a page's composition (a hero). Bind `v-model:open` to remember or restore the choice (`close` still fires with the click).

props.name: value
props.doc: The prompt copied to the clipboard on activation.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible text and accessible name while idle; empty uses the catalog's `Copy prompt`.

props.name: copiedLabel
props.doc: Visible text announced after a copy; empty uses the catalog's `Copied`.

props.name: agents
props.doc: The agents whose marks follow the label, in order; each is `{ name, icon?, logo? }`, drawn from `logo` through `Logo` when set and from the `icon` glyph otherwise; an empty list draws no marks.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables the button; `copy` is not emitted.

props.name: closable
props.doc: Shows a dismiss button beside the chip; activating it removes both from the layout and emits `close`.

events.name: copy
events.notes: Fires with the click and `value` after the clipboard write succeeds. When the write is refused, the copy fallback popover opens instead.

events.name: close
events.notes: Fires with the click on the dismiss button (`closable`), after the chip removes itself; whether it stays away is the page's decision.
